question: Why does imagining the steps toward a goal help more than imagining the moment of success?
answer: Because rehearsing the steps prepares the work, while picturing the win can feel like arriving. Pham and Taylor had students facing an exam imagine either how they would study or the joy of seeing a good grade: the process group studied more and scored better. Picture the training session, not the podium.
move: Imagine the next steps you will take, not the applause.
ask: When I daydream about a goal, do I picture the work it takes or only the finish line?
source: Pham & Taylor, Pers Soc Psychol Bull, 1999
reference: Lien B. Pham & Shelley E. Taylor, From thought to action: effects of process- versus outcome-based mental simulations on performance, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 1999
